nc_main_climbing_areas.blurb: These are the principal cliffs of Crowders Mountain, a state park in Gaston County, North Carolina, roughly 30 miles west of Charlotte. The rock is quartzite and is generally solid. Trad leads make up most of the climbing, with a smaller number of bolted lines and a few top-ropes, plus a handful of easy boulder problems. Grades cluster between 5.8 and 5.10, with a fair number of easier leads below that and a thin tail of 5.11 and 5.12. Walls such as Red Wall, David's Castle Wall and Practice Wall face east or west, so sun and shade swing with the hour, and thick leaf cover can make it hard to find warm rock. It is a busy, sociable place on weekends.

wy_fairfield_hill.blurb: Fairfield Hill is a limestone sport cliff in Sinks Canyon above Lander, Wyoming, separated from the main canyon wall by a break and divided into west, central and east sections. Every climb is bolted. Grades run from the easy 5.6 range up to a few hard test pieces, but the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.12. The style is steep and pocketed, with crimps, overhangs, a large roof and some gentler slabs that reward careful footwork. The stone is mostly good, though one cave has a reputation for looser rock. The cliff faces south, which makes sunny winter days excellent above the cold valley air; summers run hot, so early or evening sessions work better. It stays quiet compared with other Wyoming crags.

wy_fremont_canyon.blurb: Fremont Canyon is a gorge cut by the North Platte River near Alcova, about half an hour from Casper. Walls of pink granite drop to the water; the stone is mostly sound but fractured in places, so loose blocks are a real concern and helmets make sense. Trad climbing leads, with cracks the main attraction, while bouldering and sport routes fill out the rest. Roped climbs run from roughly 5.6 to 5.13, with most between 5.9 and 5.11, and lengths from about 40 to over 400 feet. Boulder problems are mostly V0 to V6. Many routes are reached from above, so rope skills matter. Spring through fall is the season, and the shoulder months are often the best. The Bridge and the mostly sport Love Shack are two of the larger sectors.

ca_foreplay_bouldering.blurb: Foreplay is the most developed bouldering on Fairview Mountain, in the High Desert near Apple Valley, California, at roughly 3,500 feet. Almost everything here is a boulder problem, spread across dozens of small clusters and single blocks on a hillside. The grades are friendly: most problems fall between V0 and V3, V4 and V5 are well represented, and only a few go harder. A circuit leads from the parking area past blocks such as Pac Man Boulder and Diamond Boulder, and groupings like Campground Cluster, Downtown and Bed Rock City hold the most problems. Because the ground is sloped, landings matter, and climbers are encouraged to improve poor ones when they open a new problem.

nm_northern_box_areas.blurb: The northern section of the Box, a canyon of rhyolite cliffs and boulders near Socorro, New Mexico. The stone is of mixed quality: much of it is solid, but some faces are loose. Sport climbing is the main draw, mostly bolted lines from about 5.9 to 5.12, with a few routes that want some gear. Bouldering is also strong, with problems mostly in the V0 to V4 range, and there are a number of top-ropes as well. Red Wall and Waterfall Wall are among the bigger walls. Winter is a good time on mild days, while summer is hot and buggy, though shade exists and many sport faces are pleasant in the morning.

tn_king_s_bluff.blurb: King's Bluff is a limestone bluff above the Cumberland River at Clarksville, Tennessee, about 45 minutes from Nashville. Nearly all of it is sport climbing, with a few trad lines and one boulder problem. Walls stand roughly 35 to 70 feet tall, and the rock offers small edges, pockets and flexing flakes. Grades run from about 5.4 to 5.12, with the greatest concentration from 5.8 to 5.11, so it suits climbers at many levels, though some find the grades stiff. The cliff faces south, giving direct sun in winter, while summer overgrowth brings shade. Larger sectors include The Orchard, The Quiet Zone and The Alley, and it is usually uncrowded.
